heading: ZIP Archive Extractor Online
introduction:
ZIP files are commonly used to share multiple documents, images, videos, and other files in one archive. They help keep related files together and make it easier to transfer a collection as a single package. However, you need to extract the archive before you can access and use its individual contents.

A ZIP extractor allows you to open a ZIP archive and retrieve the files stored inside it. File Compresser provides an online ZIP Extractor that lets you select a supported archive, extract its contents, and download the files directly through your browser.

You do not need to install a separate extraction program or create an account to use the tool. The extraction process runs on your device, so your selected archive does not need to be uploaded to an external server.

sections.heading: What Is a ZIP Extractor?
sections.body:
A ZIP extractor is a tool that opens a ZIP archive and makes its stored files available for use. When someone combines several files into a ZIP archive, the items are packaged together. Extraction reverses this process and returns the individual files.

For example, if you receive a ZIP file containing a collection of reports, images, and documents, you can extract the archive to access those items separately.

File Compresser's ZIP Extractor supports ZIP archives. After extraction, you can download individual files or download the extracted contents together as a combined ZIP file.

sections.heading: How to Extract a ZIP File Online
sections.body:
You can open a supported ZIP archive using File Compresser without installing desktop software. Follow these steps:

1. Open the ZIP Extractor page on File Compresser.
2. Select the ZIP archive from your device.
3. Start the extraction process.
4. Wait while the browser checks and extracts the archive.
5. Review the available files.
6. Download individual files or choose the combined ZIP download when several files are available.

Before downloading, review the extracted file names and make sure the archive contains the items you expected. This is particularly useful when working with project folders or documents received from another person.

sections.heading: Why Use an Online ZIP Extractor?
sections.body: An online ZIP extractor can be useful when you receive compressed files and need quick access to their contents.

sections.heading: Open ZIP Files Without Installing Software
sections.body: You may not want to install a separate application just to open one archive. A browser-based ZIP extractor provides another way to access supported ZIP files.

sections.heading: Access Individual Files
sections.body: A ZIP archive may contain many different items. Extraction allows you to access the documents, images, and other files separately instead of keeping everything inside one compressed package.

sections.heading: Download Only the Files You Need
sections.body: Sometimes you do not need every item inside an archive. File Compresser lets you download individual extracted files, which can help when you only need a specific document or image.

sections.heading: Manage Project Resources
sections.body: Developers, designers, students, and office teams often receive project files in ZIP format. Extracting the archive makes it easier to access the resources needed for a task.

sections.heading: Review Shared Documents
sections.body: If someone sends you a ZIP archive containing reports, presentations, or other documents, you can extract the contents and review the individual files.

sections.heading: Download Individual Files or a Combined ZIP
sections.body:
After extraction, you can choose how to download the available contents.

If you only need one item, downloading an individual file can save time and avoid storing unnecessary files. This may be useful when an archive contains several documents but you only need one report.

If you want to keep the extracted collection together, you can download the contents as a combined ZIP file. This option is useful when you plan to move the files to another device or share the collection again.

Remember that extracting a ZIP archive does not reduce the size of its contents. Extraction simply opens the archive and makes its stored files available. The total extracted size may be larger than the original ZIP file because the archive contains compressed data.

sections.heading: Which Archive Formats Are Supported?
sections.body:
File Compresser's current extraction tool is designed for ZIP files. It does not support every archive format.

The current workflow does not support RAR or 7z files. Encrypted archives, split archives, and ZIP64 archives are also not supported.

If you receive an archive in one of these formats, you will need a compatible extraction application. Changing the file extension does not convert an unsupported archive into a standard ZIP file.

The maximum supported input size for the ZIP Extractor is 150 MB. Make sure your archive is within this limit before starting the process.

sections.heading: How File Compresser Handles ZIP Archive Safety
sections.body:
ZIP archives can contain many files and folder paths. Some archives may also be created in ways that cause problems when their contents are extracted.

File Compresser checks archive entries and rejects unsafe paths, duplicate names, invalid integrity data, and excessive file expansion. These checks help prevent common archive extraction problems.

For example, the tool checks for path patterns that could attempt to place extracted files outside the intended destination. It also checks for absolute paths, drive letters, control characters, and Windows reserved file names.

The extractor includes protection against archives that expand to an unusually large amount of data compared with their compressed size. This helps reduce the risk of processing archive bombs, including cases with a compression ratio above 100 times.

These checks improve extraction safety, but they do not guarantee that every file inside an archive is harmless. Extracted files may still contain unsafe or unwanted content. Only open files from sources you trust, and use appropriate security software when checking unfamiliar downloads.

sections.heading: Extract ZIP Files Privately in Your Browser
sections.body:
File Compresser processes supported ZIP archives directly in your browser. Your selected archive does not need to be uploaded to an external server for extraction, and you do not need to create an account to use the tool.

The input file limit is 150 MB. The general processing queue supports up to 500 files and a combined queue size of up to 300 MB, subject to the tool's archive and extraction limits.

Processing capacity can also depend on your device and browser. Large archives with many files or a high amount of extracted data may require more memory and processing time.
